extraction.name: EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification
extraction.description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images. The dataset is used for land use and land cover classification benchmarks using deep Convolutional Neural Networks.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.publisher: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI), TU Kaiserslautern
extraction.citeAs: Helber, P., Bischke, B., Dengel, A., & Borth, D. (2019). EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were gathered from European cities distributed in over 34 countries via Amazon S3. Images were selected based on low cloud levels and recorded throughout the year to maximize variance. Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from these satellite images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentinel-2A satellite images provided by the European Space Agency (ESA) under the Copernicus program, accessed via Amazon S3.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from the satellite imagery. Bands with lower spatial resolution (20m) were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation. Atmospheric correction was not applied.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times. Mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice were sorted out and discarded. Images with color casts due to atmospheric effects were kept to advocate the classifier to learn these cases.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of 10 land use and land cover classes based on the European Urban Atlas. Labels were assigned based on the visual content of the patches. The ground truth was corrected by manually checking images and sorting out mislabeled ones.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset opens a gate towards Earth observation applications such as agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change monitoring, urban development, and environmental monitoring. It can assist in improving geographical maps and detecting land use/cover changes like deforestation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. There is a low positive correlation between classes, with agricultural classes and residential/industrial building classes being most common to each other.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The spatial resolution is 10 meters per pixel, which is lower than some benchmark datasets, making it difficult to distinguish fine details like individual churches or schools. The dataset is limited to European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Use cases include land use and land cover classification, change detection, and assisting in updating geographical maps like OpenStreetMap.
